results.sentence: TheSinging.Bible, which launched on Aug 25, added an iPhone app on Sept 21, a round-the-clock YouTube radio stream on Oct 2 and an Android app on Oct 4.
results.evidence: Launched Aug 25, 2026; App Store since Sept 21; YouTube radio since Oct 2; Google Play since Oct 4.

results.sentence: As of Oct 4, it lists 52,316 recordings: all 1,189 chapters in 22 styles, each sung in a male and a female voice.
results.evidence: 'As of October 4, 2026'; 52,316 recordings; 22 styles; 44 versions per chapter (every style in male and female voices).

results.sentence: Answered Faith reported in September that it launched with 38,048 recordings.
results.evidence: 'launched August 25 with 38,048 recordings spanning all 1,189 chapters'. (AF also says 16 styles/32 renditions at launch; not used in draft.)

results.sentence: On Oct 8, Crosswalk ran a guest commentary on The Music Bible, an app led by founder Micah Fiechter.
results.evidence: Crosswalk names Fiechter as leading a 70-person team; 'founder' is supported by themusicbible.org/ai-transparency (Founder and CEO).

results.sentence: Drawing on Fiechter's account, it reported the whole Bible in 11 styles, more than 30,000 songs and three genres in Spanish.
results.evidence: 11 styles is attributed to Fiechter ('Fiechter stated'); '30,000 songs' and 'three genres in Spanish' are the article's own statements, not attributed to Fiechter.
results.fix: On Oct 8, Crosswalk reported Fiechter saying the whole Bible is available in 11 styles; it also put the app at more than 30,000 songs, with three genres in Spanish.

results.sentence: Three days later, the headline of Fiechter's own op-ed put the figure at 38,000.
results.evidence: Oct 11, 2026 headline: 'How 38,000 AI songs might be the biggest shift in Bible access since Gutenberg'.

results.sentence: The app's homepage counter now reads 38,556.
results.evidence: Elementor counter data-to-value="38556" labelled Scripture Songs (renders from 0; value is in page source).

results.sentence: The counts differ by source and date, and no outside group has checked them.
results.evidence: First half is supported. 'No outside group has checked them' is an uncited absence claim.
results.fix: The counts differ by source and date, and we found no outside check of them.

results.sentence: Table: TheSinging.Bible 52,316 recordings; 22 styles, two voices each; English text 'Singing Bible Edition,' based on Berean Standard Bible; 'AI-empowered technologies', tools not named; Free, no sign-up, no ads.
results.evidence: All match facts page ('The Singing Bible Edition (SBE), based on the Berean Standard Bible'; 'produced with AI-empowered technologies'; 'free, no sign-up, no ads'). Tools not named on the page.

results.sentence: Table: Music Bible 38,556 songs; 14 complete-Bible genres, counting Spanish.
results.evidence: Counters 38556 and 14 (Complete Bible Genres); genre list shows 11 English + 3 Spanish.

results.sentence: Table: AI tools 'Suno and ChatGPT'.
results.evidence: Page says 'utilizes AI platforms including Suno and ChatGPT'; the list may not be complete.

results.sentence: Table: Cost, Free on iOS and Android.
results.evidence: 'can be downloaded for free on iOS and Android'.

results.sentence: Table: English text 'Not named on the pages we read'.
results.evidence: Neither homepage nor AI Transparency page names an English translation.

results.sentence: Both teams say AI shapes the music, not the words.
results.evidence: Only The Music Bible says this (AI Transparency page). TheSinging.Bible's pages say only that recordings follow the written text and were produced with 'AI-empowered technologies'; it makes no AI-shapes-music-only statement.
results.fix: The Music Bible says AI shapes the music, not the words. TheSinging.Bible says its recordings follow the written text.

results.sentence: The Music Bible pledges it 'will never use artificial intelligence to create songs that interpret, paraphrase, or extrapolate the meaning of Scripture'.
results.evidence: Exact.

results.sentence: It says verses stay in order with no choruses, though 'occasionally, a word or phrase may be repeated for musical expression'.
results.evidence: Exact; page also says 'not repeated' for verses, 'no choruses'.

results.sentence: TheSinging.Bible says 'every recording follows the written text, which is shown with every chapter'.
results.evidence: Exact.

results.sentence: The project says producers, engineers and quality-control reviewers were responsible for reviewing the recordings.
results.evidence: AF: 'The project says producers, engineers, quality-control reviewers, managers and digital specialists remained responsible for managing and reviewing the recordings.' Attributed to the release via AF.

results.sentence: 'We don't change Scripture to fit music; we change music to fit Scripture,' Fiechter told Crosswalk.
results.evidence: Exact quote.

results.sentence: The Music Bible argues that setting the whole Bible, 'over 750,000 words,' to music was more than any single artist or team could do by hand.
results.evidence: 'the practical scope of setting the entire Bible, over 750,000 words, to music has as of 2025 exceeded what any single artist or team could accomplish.' 'By hand' is paraphrase; acceptable.

results.sentence: Both projects are built for listening and memorizing.
results.evidence: Music Bible homepage lists 'Memorize'; TheSinging.Bible pages do not describe memorizing (fun facts: listening, reading along, plans).
results.fix: Both projects are built for listening; The Music Bible also pitches memorizing.

results.sentence: TheSinging.Bible says under 20 minutes a day sings a listener through the whole Bible in a year, with the text on screen.
results.evidence: 'Under 20 minutes of listening a day sings you through the entire Bible in one year'; 'View Bible Text' shows text while playing.

results.sentence: Its book of Jonah is even available as a sea shanty.
results.evidence: 'Jonah is available as a sea shanty.' (Sea Shanty/Pirate style).

results.sentence: The Music Bible app offers read-along lyrics and playlists that AI builds from a short text request.
results.evidence: 'lyrics on screen', 'read along', 'Describe the kind of playlist you want and AI will create it for you'.

results.sentence: 'I don't want people to remember Music Bible; I want them to remember the Bible,' Fiechter said.
results.evidence: Exact.

results.sentence: Neither project has published error rates.
results.evidence: AF says the TheSinging.Bible release did not publish detailed error rates; Music Bible page gives none. Absence across both is unverified by a primary source.
results.fix: We found no published error rates from either project.

results.sentence: Answered Faith noted the release did not 'publish detailed error rates from its quality-control process'.
results.evidence: Exact.

results.sentence: The Music Bible commits to 'at least 100% accuracy in the oral representation of each passage,' but its page describes no review method.
results.evidence: Exact quote; page describes no review method (note prior issue 2026-09-30 cites a 'flagged songs pulled within 24 hours' claim from elsewhere, so 'its page' wording is right).

results.sentence: TheSinging.Bible's one million plays in two weeks come from its own analytics, and 'a play should not be confused with a unique listener or a completed chapter'.
results.evidence: Exact; second clause is AF's editorial caution, not the project's. Wording acceptable.

results.sentence: On Oct 6, Barna reported that 33% of Protestant pastors feel positive about AI writing worship songs and 29% about AI interpreting scripture, compared with 64% for AI creating small-group curriculum.
results.evidence: Oct 6, 2026; worship songs 33%, interpreting scripture 29%, curriculum for small groups or Bible studies 64%.

results.sentence: The survey of 442 pastors was conducted online in December 2025.
results.evidence: 'U.S. Protestant pastors survey (n=442) was conducted online in December 2025'.

results.sentence: Barna did not ask about sung Scripture.
results.evidence: No mention of sung Scripture or music-setting in the article's reported items; absence claim limited to the published article. Consider 'does not report'.

results.sentence: These projects say AI writes only the music, so they fall between its categories.
results.evidence: Same overclaim as above; only The Music Bible makes this statement.
results.fix: The Music Bible says AI writes only the music, so it falls between these categories.

results.sentence: In June, Deseret News reported that Come and See uses an AI app for a first-pass translation of The Chosen in minority languages, 'followed by a meticulous review from subject matter experts to ensure quality and accuracy'.
results.evidence: June 1, 2026; quote exact.

results.sentence: Speech-to-speech AI then lays the original actor's voice over recordings made by linguists.
results.evidence: Matches ('overlay the sound of the original voice actor onto the audio provided by linguists').

results.sentence: The goal is 600 languages, more than 500 of them with no existing dubbing infrastructure.
results.evidence: Matches. Note: item is from June 1, outside the Sep 17-Oct 17 coverage window and not 'past month'; the draft does date it 'In June'. Editorial call.

results.sentence: At Gloo's fourth annual AI hackathon, held Oct 6-8, Biola University's team Holy Sound reached the finals with a tool that lets people run a church sound board in natural language.
results.evidence: 'fourth annual hackathon... Boulder... Oct. 6-8'; 'made it to the finals'; natural-language sound boards.

results.sentence: It is designed to help non-technical volunteers use Ableton Live during services, and it remains a hackathon prototype.
results.evidence: Source: 'specifically designed to help non-technical people use Ableton Live during church services'. 'Volunteers' is an embellishment ('people'); 'remains a hackathon prototype' is not stated anywhere in the source.
results.fix: It is designed to help non-technical people use Ableton Live during church services.

results.sentence: Duke Taber quotes: 'Pastors should also make clear that a musical performance is not a new form of biblical authority. Melody involves interpretation'; AI 'can mispronounce names, place emphasis in strange locations or produce a musical mood that fights against a passage's meaning'; plays 'cannot measure repentance, understanding, obedience or growing love for Christ'.
results.evidence: All three exact. Taber is bylined author.

results.sentence: Kenny Lamm of NC Baptists drew the line in January: AI 'can assist the craft but cannot replace the heart and witness of human worshippers'.
results.evidence: Exact; Lamm is Worship Ministries strategist for North Carolina Baptists; article Jan 3, 2026. He told Baptist Press.

results.evidence: Frontmatter text matches WEB from bible-api exactly; quoted phrases in Reflection are exact substrings.

results.evidence: Scripture reference claim; Deut 6:5 'heart, soul, might'; Matt 22:37-38 greatest commandment. Uncited but scriptural.

results.sentence: Paul tells believers to let the word of Christ dwell in them richly as they teach one another with psalms, hymns and spiritual songs (Colossians 3:16).
results.evidence: Consistent with Col 3:16 (also quoted in sources 1 and 2).

results.sentence: Dek/description: Two teams say AI now sings every chapter of Scripture without changing the text.
results.evidence: Supported by both projects' own claims (attributed as 'say').

results.evidence: Editorial/theological opinion, not factual claim.
